children: Bank of America thinks the semiconductor industry is likely to get much bigger, and the top producer of AI accelerators, Nvidia Corp. (NVDA, Financials), is sitting in the heart of it.
The bank predicts semiconductor sales to rise from roughly $1.7 trillion in 2026 to $3.2 trillion in 2030. That's almost double in four years.
Despite all the recent talk of AI spending eventually cooling, we don't see much evidence of that yet, BofA writes.
Customer orders are still robust. Capacity still available. The bank says 2027 is largely booked out with computing, networking and memory vendors and 2028 is also looking tight.

Memory plays a large element in the plot. BofA predicts the market would expand from $937 billion to $1.8 trillion by 2030. The server market might grow from $359 billion to $848 billion. That leaves a lot of firms with an interest.

BofA highlighted compute names Nvidia and AMD, networking Marvell and analog chips Analog Devices and onsemi. If momentum continues, Micron, Lam Research, Applied Materials and Intel might be on the receiving end.
BofA makes the opposite case for investors worried the AI chip cycle is running out of room. The next test is a simple one: can those packed order books stay packed as the industry enters 2027?

title: The chip market may be heading for a $3.2 trillion transformation
